title: Short link service
prompt: Design a service that turns long URLs into short links and redirects visitors reliably. Discuss creation, read traffic, expiry, and abuse.
clarify: How many links are created and opened each day?
Are custom aliases, expiry, or analytics required?
What availability and redirect latency matter?
rubric: Defines APIs and a stable short-code strategy
Chooses a data model and handles collisions
Explains cache, scale, and redirect latency
Covers abuse, expiry, failure, and observability

title: Notification delivery
prompt: Design a platform that sends email, push, and in-app notifications from product events. Handle user preferences, retries, and spikes.
clarify: What delivery channels and volume are expected?
How fresh must notifications be?
Can users opt out or set quiet hours?
rubric: Separates event intake from channel workers
Models preferences and idempotent delivery
Plans retries, dead letters, and rate limits
Explains observability and delivery guarantees

title: Group chat messages
prompt: Design text messaging for group chats across web and mobile clients. Discuss ordering, offline delivery, and large groups.
clarify: How large can a group become?
What ordering guarantee is needed?
Should offline messages sync across devices?
rubric: Defines message and conversation APIs
Explains ordering and unique message IDs
Handles online fanout and offline sync
Addresses storage growth, failures, and abuse

title: Activity feed
prompt: Design a home feed showing recent posts from accounts a user follows. Discuss ranking, pagination, and users with many followers.
clarify: Is the feed chronological or ranked?
How many follows and posts per user?
How fresh must new posts appear?
rubric: Defines feed and post data models
Compares fanout on write and read
Uses stable pagination and caching
Handles celebrity accounts and stale results

title: Payment event ledger
prompt: Design an internal ledger that records payment state changes and supports reconciliation. Prevent duplicate processing and preserve an audit trail.
clarify: Which systems produce payment events?
How quickly must balances be visible?
What reconciliation and retention rules apply?
rubric: Defines immutable events and state transitions
Uses idempotency keys and transactional boundaries
Plans reconciliation and recovery
Covers access control, audit, and monitoring

title: Large file processing
prompt: Design uploads of large files followed by virus scanning, conversion, and download. Handle retries and a user-visible status.
clarify: What file sizes and formats are supported?
How long can processing take?
Who can access each output?
rubric: Uses direct, resumable uploads and metadata
Models asynchronous jobs and states
Handles retries, quarantine, and cleanup
Secures access and observes failures

title: Product analytics pipeline
prompt: Design ingestion of product events and dashboards for daily active users and funnels. Discuss late events and privacy.
clarify: What is the event volume and retention period?
How fresh must dashboards be?
Are user deletion and consent required?
rubric: Defines event schema and ingestion contract
Separates raw storage from aggregates
Handles duplicates, late data, and backfills
Covers privacy, access, and data quality

title: Background job queue
prompt: Design a queue for background tasks with delayed work, retries, and multiple workers. Discuss delivery guarantees and stuck jobs.
clarify: What throughput and latency are expected?
Can jobs run more than once?
Are ordering or priorities required?
rubric: Defines enqueue, lease, ack, and retry flows
Explains at-least-once delivery and idempotency
Handles dead letters and stalled workers
Plans scaling and operational visibility

title: Resolve a team disagreement
prompt: Tell a specific story about a technical disagreement. Explain the stakes, how you listened, the decision, and the result.
clarify: What did each person value?
What evidence changed the decision?
What would you do differently now?
rubric: Sets concrete context and your role
Describes actions you personally took
Shows how disagreement was resolved
Gives an outcome and a lesson

title: Learn from a failed release
prompt: Tell a specific story about a release or project that did not go as planned. Explain your responsibility, response, and learning.
clarify: What was the impact?
What did you communicate and fix first?
Which process changed afterward?
rubric: Owns a specific mistake without blame
Explains response and communication
Shows measurable or observable recovery
Names a lasting preventive change

title: Navigate an unclear requirement
prompt: Describe a time you had to make progress with an unclear request. Explain the questions you asked, decisions you made, and result.
clarify: Who needed the outcome?
Which assumption was most risky?
How did you validate direction early?
rubric: Defines the ambiguity and its impact
Shows deliberate questions and assumptions
Explains a small validation step
Reports result and what changed

title: Make a difficult tradeoff
prompt: Describe a decision where speed, quality, cost, or scope conflicted. Explain the options and the tradeoff you chose.
clarify: Who was affected by each option?
What evidence did you have?
How did you monitor the result?
rubric: States the alternatives fairly
Explains decision criteria and constraints
Shows stakeholder communication
Reflects on the outcome and limits
